clue.text: Remove foil and allay suspicion

definitions.meaning: to take away someone's weapon, a foil being a fencing sword
to win over or calm a doubting person, as in charming a critic

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to strip of weapons and, figuratively, to win over and remove hostility.

clue.text: Limit a bleeper — part can be taken off

indicators.note: only part of the words limit a bleeper is used, a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: Instructions for removing a section of a pager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken off' is the mimic's sense, as a comedian takes off a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic them, so something copyable qualifies.

clue.text: Withering, like Shelley's deep tone

definitions.meaning: fading and decaying, like leaves in the fall
Shelley's Ode to the West Wind speaks of 'a deep

explanation.definitionFit: The fall season is when plants fade and wither, and Shelley's poem uses this very adjective for the deep tone.

clue.text: Show ring and give promises of party

parts.note: to show is to manifest
a ring is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A display of a wedding ring as a pledge at a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A political party publishes its pledges in a programme document before an election.

clue.text: Well-known climber, I scale Mt Tumbledown

indicators.note: something tumbledown has collapsed into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A famous mountaineer announces an ascent of Mount Tumbledown.
explanation.walkthrough: Mount Tumbledown is a real peak in the Falklands, which makes 'climber' look like a mountaineer; it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This garden vine is a familiar climbing plant on walls and trellises.

clue.text: Where striker stands defiant, not easily ruffled

parts.note: in cricket the batsman facing (the striker) stands at the crease, a line marked on the pitch
defiant means resistant

explanation.surface: A batsman at the wicket stays calm and defiant.
explanation.walkthrough: The crease is the line in cricket where the batsman stands; 'not easily ruffled' is used of fabric, not temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric that resists wrinkles stays smooth, so it is hard to ruffle.

clue.text: Duck-doctor takes all morning to go round

indicators.note: to go round is to turn about, so the whole string of doctor, all and morning is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
AM stands for ante meridiem, the morning

explanation.surface: A vet specialising in ducks makes a morning-long round of visits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go round' turns the whole run DRALLAM backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the commonest wild duck, the drake with a green head.

clue.text: 14th century appears modern in outskirts of Torino

indicators.note: in means the letters for modern sit inside the outer pair
the outskirts of a town are its edges, so the first and last letters of Torino are taken

parts.note: modern means recent

explanation.surface: Fourteenth-century buildings looking new on the edge of Turin.
explanation.walkthrough: Torino is the Italian name for Turin, apt for an Italian art term.
explanation.definitionFit: In Italian art history the term names the 1300s, the century of Giotto.

clue.text: Does an agent put it into orbit?

definitions.text: Does an agent put it into orbit?

parts.words: Does an agent put it into orbit?
parts.note: orbit is the eye socket, so a secret agent screwing in a telescope-like lens is the joke, not a space launch

explanation.definitionFit: A small hand telescope, which one holds up to an eye.

clue.text: I stand corrected, in front of church, for aloofness

indicators.note: in front of places the rearranged letters before the abbreviation for church
corrected means put right, so the letters of I stand are rearranged

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone admits being wrong outside a church, standing apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrected' turns I STAND into DISTAN, which goes before CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotional reserve is a coolness that keeps others at arm's length.

clue.text: Tired agent taking shelter inside

indicators.note: taking means the word for agent takes in another word
inside confirms that shelter goes within the letters for agent

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
a lee is a sheltered side, out of the wind

explanation.surface: An exhausted spy takes refuge indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Being drowsy is how a weary person feels.

clue.text: Duffer's on the organ — better wear these!

indicators.note: on puts the word for duffer's after the organ in an across answer

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing
a muff is a clumsy person, a duffer, so duffer's becomes muff's

explanation.surface: A bad organist is playing, so protect your hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: A muff is a bungler; the possessive gives MUFFS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ear coverings are what one would wear against the din of a poor organist.

clue.text: This nurse a' valiant leader in dungeon

indicators.note: in places the a and the leading letter inside the prison room

parts.note: a dungeon is a cell

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the first letter of valiant is used

explanation.surface: A brave nurse leads from a dungeon.
explanation.walkthrough: Edith Cavell was a British nurse executed by the Germans in 1915 for helping Allied soldiers escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Cavell was a famous British wartime nurse, so the definition names her.

clue.text: Variegated star does break up .

indicators.note: break up means fall to pieces, so the letters of star does are rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrity's actions shatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mixed and varied things are of several kinds, like a variegated assortment.

clue.text: Bedeck a king in this demi-paradise

indicators.note: in places a and king inside the country

parts.note: John of Gaunt in Shakespeare's Richard II calls England 'this other Eden, demi-paradise'
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: Decorating a monarch in a near-Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from John of Gaunt's speech in Richard II.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck with garlands is to adorn with wreaths of flowers.

clue.text: Knockdown said to be fatal

definitions.meaning: to strike someone to the ground

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to strike down, and the old adjective means cruel or deadly.

clue.text: Just lies sprawled out in a kind of sweater

parts.note: just means fair

indicators.note: sprawled out means spread untidily, so the letters of lies are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone simply lounges about in a jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprawled out' turns LIES into ISLE; the sweater is a patterned knit from the Shetland island of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: This patterned knitted jumper is named after a Shetland island.

clue.text: Crumbs! Svengali. has gone mad

definitions.note: here a noun, leftover bits, not the exclamation

indicators.note: gone mad means become disordered, so the letters of Svengali are rearranged

explanation.surface: A startled cry: the hypnotist Svengali has lost his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbs!' looks like a British exclamation of surprise; it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftovers or scraps remaining after a meal are like crumbs.

clue.text: Cries of distress or just one about Beachy Head?

indicators.note: about means the call for help goes round the other letter

parts.note: one single cry of distress is the Morse signal SOS

indicators.note: a head is at the top, so the first letter of Beachy is used

explanation.surface: A distress call near a cliff on the English coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Beachy Head is a chalk cliff in Sussex; its head gives B, inside SOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeping noises are cries made in distress.

clue.text: Pen-pusher — possibly, a royal official

parts.note: a pen is a female swan, so one who drives swans along is the keeper of the Crown's swans, not a clerk

explanation.definitionFit: A keeper of swans, an office held for the Crown on the Thames.

clue.text: Straddle top mount

parts.note: top means best
to mount a horse is to ride it

explanation.surface: Advice to sit astride the finest horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit with legs either side of something is to straddle it.

clue.text: Nick shows, how goose is cooked

indicators.note: cooked means doctored or falsified, so the letters of how goose are rearranged

explanation.surface: A demonstration of how to prepare a goose.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick is British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are slang for a jail.

clue.text: How monotonous to sing wordlessly with regular beat

parts.note: to hum is to sing with closed lips
a drum beat is a steady rhythm

explanation.surface: A complaint that humming to a steady beat is dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull routine is tedious and unvarying.

clue.text: Restore retired premier to 'state

indicators.note: retired means gone back, so the letters for premier and state are read backwards

parts.note: PM is the Prime Minister, the premier
to aver is to state

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister is brought back to office.
explanation.definitionFit: To renovate something is to give it a new look, restoring it.

clue.text: Walpole's'ability' to 'strike lucky : banishes depression in peace

indicators.note: banishes means sends away, so the letters for depression are taken out

parts.note: Horace Walpole coined the word for a knack of happy accidental discoveries
a dip is a depression in the ground

explanation.surface: Walpole's good luck ends gloom and brings calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm tranquillity is a state of peace.

clue.text: Guard transported by rail

indicators.note: by places the railway letters next to it

parts.note: transported means sent
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A guard is carried along by train.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier on watch at a post is a guard.

clue.text: Don, for example, is so impractical

definitions.meaning: a don is a university teacher
concerned with theory rather than real use

explanation.definitionFit: A university lecturer is a scholar, and the adjective also means merely theoretical.

clue.text: First of eleven players in Orient has right of way.

indicators.note: in places the first letter and the players inside the compass point

parts.note: the Orient is the East

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so eleven gives its first letter

parts.note: players in a team are men

explanation.surface: A football team's first player in Orient gets a free path.
explanation.walkthrough: Leyton Orient is a London football club, which makes 'eleven players' look like a team.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal right over another's land, such as a path across it, is a right of way.

clue.text: A fair vehicle but over-powered

parts.note: the bumper car at a funfair takes its electric power from an overhead grid, not an excessive engine

explanation.definitionFit: A small electric bumper car at a funfair, fed from a ceiling grid.
